questions.q: Why does Northbridge Retail consider HashiCorp Vault alongside Key Vault and Secrets Manager?
options: Vault is required by law for multi-cloud companies
Vault is cloud-agnostic, giving one consistent secrets API and access model across both Azure (AKS) and AWS (EKS) workloads
Vault is free while Key Vault and Secrets Manager are not
Vault replaces the need for any IAM or RBAC system
questions.explain: Key Vault and Secrets Manager are each tied to their own cloud, while Vault runs independently and authenticates workloads from any environment through pluggable auth methods.

questions.q: What is a "secrets engine" in Vault?
options: A single, fixed key/value store with no other options
A pluggable component, mounted at its own path, handling a specific category of secret (KV, database, PKI, transit, etc.)
A hardware device used to generate secrets
A synonym for an IAM policy
questions.explain: Vault organizes functionality around secrets engines — pluggable, independently-mounted components like the KV engine, database engine, PKI engine, and transit engine.

questions.q: What advantage does Vault's database secrets engine offer over simple scheduled rotation?
options: It eliminates the need for a database entirely
It generates a brand-new, short-lived credential per request with automatic expiration, rather than rotating one long-lived shared credential on a timer
It only works with NoSQL databases
It requires manual password changes every day
questions.explain: Dynamic secrets issue a unique credential per request with a lease duration and automatic revocation, so there's no long-lived shared credential to rotate in the first place.

questions.q: What does the "mount path" determine when enabling a secrets engine?
options: The physical server location of the Vault cluster
The API route at which that secrets engine is reachable
The expiration date of every secret in that engine
The number of users allowed to access Vault
questions.explain: The mount path is the API route an engine is enabled at — for example "secret/" by default, or a custom path like "sre-secrets".

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend KV version 2 over version 1 for nearly every new mount?
options: Version 1 has been completely removed from Vault
Version 2 adds data versioning, check-and-set to prevent accidental overwrites, and soft-delete
Version 2 is required for all database credentials
There is no practical difference between the two versions
questions.explain: KV version 2 provides safety features — versioning, check-and-set, and soft-delete — that version 1's simpler, non-versioned store doesn't offer.
